item.title: WAF investigating allegation of staff member demanding fish and chicken for water supply
item.description: The Water Authority of Fiji is still investigating allegations that a team member demanded fish and chicken in exchange for supplying water to residents of Naveria in Savusavu. Speaking to fijivillage News, resident Jan Mohammed claims the team member has been going around the area and asking for the same.
item.content:encoded:
The Water Authority of Fiji is still investigating allegations that a team member demanded fish and chicken in exchange for supplying water to residents of Naveria in Savusavu.

Speaking to fijivillage News, resident Jan Mohammed claims the team member has been going around the area and asking for the same.

Mohammed says although they live in a hilly area, the road is suitable for water carting trucks to deliver water.

However, he says water carting trucks hardly visit the area, forcing him to carry buckets to town to collect water.

The resident says water carting trucks only arrived yesterday after months.

He says their well has also dried up, and no government minister has visited the area to assess their situation.

Mohammed adds that politicians only visit the area when they need votes.

item.title: Kiran urges parents to prioritise children's safety following alleged child-luring incident near Wailekutu bridge
item.description: Parents and guardians are being urged not to leave children unsupervised while selling goods along roadsides, following a viral video showing an alleged attempt to lure a child into a vehicle near Wailekutu Bridge, outside Lami. Minister for Women, Children, Social Protection and Cohesion Sashi Kiran says children selling fish, fruits and other items along busy roads face serious risks, including
item.content:encoded:
Parents and guardians are being urged not to leave children unsupervised while selling goods along roadsides, following a viral video showing an alleged attempt to lure a child into a vehicle near Wailekutu Bridge, outside Lami.

Minister for Women, Children, Social Protection and Cohesion Sashi Kiran says children selling fish, fruits and other items along busy roads face serious risks, including traffic accidents, exploitation, abuse and encounters with strangers who may harm them.

Kiran says while some families depend on extra income to support their daily needs, children's safety and wellbeing must always come first.

She stresses that parents and guardians have a responsibility to ensure children are not left alone in unsafe public places.

Kiran has condemned the alleged incident, saying no child should ever feel pressured, threatened or unsafe.

She says the matter has been reported to the Fiji Police Force, and investigations are underway.

Kiran has also praised the child for escaping the situation and the community member who stepped in to help.

She is urging anyone who witnessed the incident or has information to contact Police.

Kiran is also encouraging parents to teach their children how to recognise suspicious behaviour, refuse gifts or money from strangers, say no firmly and immediately seek help from a trusted adult.

She says protecting children is everyone's responsibility, whether at home, in school or along roadsides.

Members of the public are urged to report any child protection concerns to the 24-hour Child Helpline on 1325 or the Police toll-free helpline on 1681.

Questions have been sent to the Fiji Police Force regarding the alleged incident.

item.title: Peni Cabenalevu remanded in attempted Police murder case in Laucala Bay
item.description: The 23-year-old man who is charged with two counts of assault causing actual bodily harm and two counts of attempted murder in relation to an incident in Laucala Bay last Thursday, has been remanded. Peni Cabenalevu appeared before Suva Magistrate Joseph Daurewa this afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
The 23-year-old man who is charged with two counts of assault causing actual bodily harm and two counts of attempted murder in relation to an incident in Laucala Bay last Thursday, has been remanded.

Peni Cabenalevu appeared before Suva Magistrate Joseph Daurewa this afternoon.

It was heard in court that there are four victims, including his wife.

Prosecution has strongly objected to any bail for Cabenalevu due to the seriousness of the matter.

He has been further remanded in custody, and a Domestic Violence Restraining Order (DVRO) has also been issued.

The matter has been adjourned to 7th December, where Magistrate Daurewa will formally transfer the case to the Suva High Court.

Meanwhile, a video circulating on social media shows several people running towards a vehicle and attempting to pull the driver out. The driver is then seen attempting to drive away, hitting another vehicle in the process. He is later seen speeding towards the group of men who had tried to pull him out before hitting two police officers. The impact throws both officers into the air.

In another case that was called before Magistrate Yogesh Prasad this afternoon, Cabenalevu has been remanded in relation to the matter involving careless driving.

The case has been adjourned to 7th December for plea.

item.title: Germany extends helping hand to drought-hit Batiki Island
item.description: The German Government, through its Embassy in Suva, has provided assistance worth $24,055, including 30,600 litres of safe drinking water to help families on Batiki Island meet their daily needs. The assistance include 1,700 cartons containing 20,400 bottles of drinking water, with each bottle holding 1.5 litres.
item.content:encoded:
The German Government, through its Embassy in Suva, has provided assistance worth $24,055, including 30,600 litres of safe drinking water to help families on Batiki Island meet their daily needs.

The assistance include 1,700 cartons containing 20,400 bottles of drinking water, with each bottle holding 1.5 litres.

The Ministry of Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Risk Management has also provided funding to cover the cost of transporting the water to Batiki Island.

Batiki community member Eapi Nabou, who is from Naigani Village, says the assistance is a relief for residents who have been struggling with prolonged water shortages.

Speaking during the official handover at Narain Jetty, Nabou thanked the German Government and the Fiji Government for their support.

He says the community is grateful for the assistance provided by the German Government through its humanitarian programme.

Permanent Secretary for Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Risk Management Mitieli Cama says the water assistance is part of the Government's immediate response to the ongoing El Niño drought.

Cama says the Ministry is working closely with development partners, including the German Embassy, to ensure affected communities receive the assistance they need.

He is urging the people of Batiki to use the donated water wisely and prioritise drinking and cooking to ensure the limited supply lasts as long as possible.

Cama says the Ministry, through the Commissioner's Office, is also working with other government agencies and development partners on plans to establish boreholes to provide additional water sources for the island.

He says discussions are ongoing, with the proposed boreholes forming part of the Government's efforts to address the water shortage.

Cama adds that the Ministry is working closely with the Batiki community on its development and action plans to address the ongoing water challenges.

He says the first emergency committee meeting has been held, and a monitoring system is now in place to assess the situation in affected communities through regular reports.

Cama says these reports will help the Ministry identify communities that require further water deliveries and other assistance.

Meanwhile, the German Embassy says prolonged dry weather has put pressure on water supplies, particularly in remote island communities that depend heavily on rainfall.

They say the shortage of safe drinking water on Batiki has also raised serious health concerns, with the Ministry of Health reporting an increase in diarrhoeal illnesses on the island earlier this year .

The Embassy says the assistance follows a direct request from the Batiki community for help in accessing safe drinking water.

Based on an estimated requirement of three litres per person per day, the donated water is expected to last approximately four weeks.

German Ambassador to Fiji Nicole Menzenbach says access to safe drinking water is essential for protecting people's health and dignity, particularly in remote island communities.

She says when the people of Batiki approached the Embassy for help, they recognised the urgency of the situation and wanted to provide practical assistance.

Menzenbach says while the donation will provide much-needed relief to families, it is only a temporary measure and cannot replace long-term solutions to water shortages.

She adds that Germany stands with the people of Batiki and other communities across Fiji facing challenges in accessing safe drinking water.

The water shipment is scheduled to reach Batiki Island this Thursday.

item.title: Batiki families struggle as water sources dry up
item.description: Families on Batiki Island in Lomaiviti Province are facing a worsening water shortage, with some households reportedly sharing a single bottle of water among five family members to get through the day. For the people of Batiki, the water crisis is no longer just a concern raised at meetings but a daily struggle affecting their families and communities. Community member Eapi Nabou, from Naigani Vil
item.content:encoded:
Families on Batiki Island in Lomaiviti Province are facing a worsening water shortage, with some households reportedly sharing a single bottle of water among five family members to get through the day. For the people of Batiki, the water crisis is no longer just a concern raised at meetings but a daily struggle affecting their families and communities. Community member Eapi Nabou, from Naigani Village, says the island's four villages and one school are heavily dependent on rainwater harvesting. He says about 90 percent of homes rely on collected rainwater for their daily needs. However, prolonged dry conditions have caused wells and surface water sources on the island to dry up. Nabou says the situation has been particularly difficult over the past five months, with families struggling to access enough water for their basic needs. He says some men have also resorted to bathing in the ocean because of the shortage. Nabou says concerns about water shortages have been raised through traditional channels for more than 20 years, with communities continuing to call for improvements to the island's existing water sources. He says while government assistance has helped with water cartage in recent months, the communities recognise that emergency assistance alone will not solve their long-standing water problems. With the support of their newly registered non-profit organisation, the Lomanitakali Foundation, the community has started exploring solutions and seeking assistance from development partners. Nabou says the community is now exploring more sustainable options, including groundwater extraction and desalination plants. He says the Mineral Resources Department has already conducted a survey and identified potential groundwater sources on the island. However, the community is now seeking government assistance with the machinery and equipment needed to transport a drilling machine to Batiki. This would allow the community to access the identified groundwater sources. Nabou says the community hopes the drilling can be carried out before their remaining water supplies run out, particularly with the expected El Niño peak in January. He says their main concern is ensuring that families back home, particularly children and the elderly, have reliable access to safe drinking water.

item.title: All G11 members have applied to contest next general elections under People's Alliance Party - Balawa
item.description: All members of the Group of 11 have applied to contest the next general election under the People's Alliance Party, with their applications currently being processed. The G11 members are Ioane Naivalurua (bloc leader), Viliame Naupoto, Mosese Bulitavu, Naisa Tuinaceva, Josaia Niudamu, Sachida Nand, Shalen Kumar, Aliki Bia, Penioni Ravunawa, Taito Rokomatu and Alipate Tuicolo.
item.content:encoded:
All members of the Group of 11 have applied to contest the next general election under the People's Alliance Party, with their applications currently being processed.

The G11 members are Ioane Naivalurua (bloc leader), Viliame Naupoto, Mosese Bulitavu, Naisa Tuinaceva, Josaia Niudamu, Sachida Nand, Shalen Kumar, Aliki Bia, Penioni Ravunawa, Taito Rokomatu and Alipate Tuicolo.

People's Alliance Party General Secretary Sila Balawa has confirmed to fijivillage News that all G11 members have submitted their applications, which is now going through the party's selection process.

Earlier this morning, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says all applications are first submitted to the General Secretary before being forwarded to the party's Selection Board, followed by the Executive Interview Board, before reaching him.

Meanwhile, the latest election-related opinion polling by the Centre for Democracy and Dialogue, involving 1,673 participants, shows the People's Alliance Party leading with 27.5 percent support.

The survey also found that 13.6 percent of respondents preferred Rabuka as their choice for Prime Minister.
